questions.question:
In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements.

**Statements:**

All pens are books.

All books are novels.

All novels are good.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some novels are pens.

II. All books are good.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.

questions.solution:
**Explanation:**

We draw a Venn diagram using the given statements:

All pens are books.

All books are novels.

All novels are good.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/179b657fad81358af590078a6287337bd84bfb8d2e26862a9902310d7260bf0a.png] 

Now we consider the given conclusions:

**I. Some novels are pens ****→ Follows** → Since 'all pens are books' and 'all books are pens' we can say that all pens are novels which can also be referred as some novels are pens and therefore the conclusion follows.

**II. All books are good ****→ Follows** → We have 'all books are novels' and 'all novels are good' so there is an indirect relation between books and good and it is safe to say that all books are good thus the conclusion follows.

So both conclusions I and II follows.

**Hence the correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question:
Three Statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All D are V.

Some S are D.

No W is a S.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some W are not D.

II. Some V are S.

III. Some D are S.

options.text: Conclusions I, II and III follow.
Both Conclusions II and III follow

questions.solution:
**Explanation:**

We draw a Venn diagram using the given statements:**
All D are V.

Some S are D.

No W is a S.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/12cc83e7ac5349ad2767738834006c7d396a2bbd032f9ec1782d0a47a15e55ee.png] 

Now we consider the given conclusions:

**I. Some W are not D ****→ Does not follow** → We have no information that suggests the relation between W and D so we cannot assume anything and therefore the conclusion does not follow.

**II. Some V are S ****→ Follows** → Since 'all D are V' and 'some S are D', it is safe to say that some S are V and vice versa so the conclusion follows.

**III. Some D are S → Follows** → We have 'some S are D' which can also be referred as some D are S and therefore the conclusion follows.

So both conclusions II and III follows.**

**Hence the correct answer is option 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] __Mistake Points__** 

**Please note that there is no direct negative relation between W and D. So we can't determine whether Some W are not D is true or not.

 

Some D are not W is true but from that, we can't conclude some W are not D is also true.**
